name: The Hill of Seven Sisters
region_detail: An isolated grassy hill beyond the established ranchlands.
site_type: stone circle | Ancient sites; supernatural sites | Ancient megalithic monument and possible burial ground.
history: Seven standing stones crown a low hill that has served as a landmark along Rathen migration routes for generations. Rathen tradition associates the stones with seven ancient queens, though different clans preserve different names and accounts of their lives. No known record establishes the identity of the monument's builders.
current_state: The hill remains undisturbed and is occasionally visited by Rathen travelers. The stones bear shallow grooves that are difficult to distinguish from weathering. Visitors sometimes find the arrangement subtly altered from their recollection; several have reported hearing women arguing after nightfall.
inhabitants: Occasional Rathen visitors; grazing animals. No permanent occupants are established.
danger_level: Low ordinarily; uncertain if the stones are disturbed or their supernatural properties are investigated.
points_of_interest:
Seven standing stones; shallow carved grooves; a flattened central area; small offerings left by travelers; low earthworks obscured beneath the grass.

Unresolved elements: Whether the stones mark actual burials.; The identity of the seven women and the language of their arguments.; Whether the stones physically change position or alter observers' perceptions.; The significance of the central area and the buried earthworks.
discovery: An isolated grassy hill beyond the established ranchlands. Rathen trailkeepers maintain an old migration route passing near the hill. Orun Wheelkeeper can direct travelers familiar with local customs.
